predecessors.note: Bahraini overlordship in 1820-1851 and the British recognition of Qatar as a dependent of Bahrain in 1861-62 are on the History of Qatar page; the Bahrain side is another dossier's (house-of-khalifa / bahrain).

land.text: Qatar, incorporated by January 1872 as a province in Najd under the sanjak of Najd, with Jassim bin Mohammed as kaymakam

successors.note: The Ottomans 'officially renounced sovereignty over Qatar in 1913'; Cliopatria's 'Qatar' row (1913-1915, qatar) is the sheikhdom again.

capitals.name: Al Bidda (Doha)
capitals.note: In 1848 Mohammed bin Thani and his tribe moved from Fuwayrit to Al Bidda; Doha grew around it. The page names no capital before 1916 and none for 1820-1847 (page silent).

keyframe_review.note: 24,587 km2 for 1820-1852: the whole Qatar peninsula (48 gazetteer cells) plus about 21 cells of the Saudi mainland coast and about 19 cells around Ras al-Khaimah and Fujairah. The History of Qatar page gives the peninsula only (the Al Khalifa 'claimed Qatar and Bahrain by 1783'); the Al Qasimi page puts the Qawasim around Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah and never mentions Qatar, so the northern patch is a Cliopatria mislabel (possibly the Qawasim) and the mainland strip is unsupported. Keep the peninsula.

keyframe_review.note: 7,851 km2 for 1853-1855: the northern 28 of the peninsula's 48 cells, the southern 20 given to the Emirate of Nejd (to 1872). The Emirate of Nejd page: after the Battle of Mesaimeer (June 1851) Faisal 'gained temporary dominion over Qatar, which was previously under Bahraini control', and in the peace of 25 July he restored Al Bidda Fort and 'agreed to stop interfering in Qatari affairs'; nothing keeps the south Najdi afterwards. The whole peninsula is Qatari again.

keyframe_review.note: 13,431 km2 for 1856-1894: Qatar's northern 28 cells plus 17 cells in the Ras al-Khaimah and Fujairah area (not Qatari, see 1820) and none of the south. Years: this shape belongs to 1856-1871; by January 1872 Qatar is an Ottoman province (Ottoman dossier), and Muhammad bin Thani was in 1863 'the acknowledged governor of the Qatar Peninsula' (Palgrave). The whole peninsula, 1856-1871.

keyframe_review.note: 5,472 km2 for 1895-1899: the Ras al-Khaimah and Fujairah patch alone; not a single Qatari cell. Qatar was an Ottoman province from January 1872 (the Ottomans 'officially renounced sovereignty over Qatar in 1913'; Jassim defeated the Ottomans at Al Wajbah in 1893 and they 'conceded defeat'), and the Ottoman dossier draws it. Draw nothing for this dossier in these years.

ledger.note: 1820: Cliopatria begins its Qatar row. The pages date no Qatari state in 1820: the Al Khalifa 'claimed Qatar and Bahrain by 1783' and 'continued to exert authority over the mainland'; Doha was razed by an East India Company vessel in 1821 and the Al-Buainain ruled it until their expulsion in 1828. Bridging at confidence 1 (Cliopatria's year).

region.text: the Qatari coast: Fuwayrit, Al Khor and Al Bidda

ledger.note: 1847: the Al Khalifa attack the Qatari coast. Muhammad bin Khalifa landed at Al Khor in November 1847, won the Battle of Fuwayrit on 17 November 1847 and demolished Al Bidda, moving its inhabitants to Bahrain; in 1848 Mohammed bin Thani settled at Al Bidda.

1851: Najd occupies Qatar for a month. After the Battle of Mesaimeer (June 1851) Faisal 'gained temporary dominion over Qatar, which was previously under Bahraini control'; Al Thani forces seized Burj Al-Maah on 8 June (History of Qatar page).

region.text: Qatar and the Al Bidda fort

ledger.note: 1851: peace of 25 July. Brokered by Saeed bin Tahnun Al Nahyan: Ali bin Khalifa pays Faisal 4,000 German krones a year as zakat, Faisal restores Al Bidda Fort and agrees to stop interfering in Qatari affairs (the page gives the day and month; the year follows the Battle of Mesaimeer).

region.text: the Qatari coast: Fuwayrit, Al Khor and Al Bidda

ledger.note: 1851: the Qatari-Bahraini conflict of 1847-1851 ends with the peace of 25 July 1851 brokered by Saeed bin Tahnun, which returned Al Bidda to Ali bin Khalifa's chieftainship (History of Qatar page); Mohammed bin Thani relinquished his position. Added by the reviewer so that the contest matches the war of 1847-1851 instead of running to 1868.

1867: the Qatari-Bahraini War. Bahrain's combined forces sacked Doha and Al Wakrah in 1867 (History of Qatar page; no month). Added by the reviewer to open the contest that the 1868 Pelly settlement closes.

1868: the British settle the quarrel. After the Qatari-Bahraini War (1867-68; Al Wakrah and Al Bidda sacked with 2,000 men, 'at the end of 1867 temporarily blotted out of existence') Lewis Pelly's 1868 settlement 'explicitly acknowledged the position of Mohammed bin Thani as an important representative of the Peninsula's tribes'; a treaty of May 1861 had recognised Qatar as a dependent of Bahrain.

region.text: Qatar, a province in Najd under the Ottoman sanjak

ledger.note: 1872: Qatar becomes an Ottoman province. The Ottomans expanded into Eastern Arabia in 1871; in December 1871 Jassim bin Mohammed authorized the Ottomans to send 100 troops to Al Bidda; 'By January 1872, the Ottomans had incorporated Qatar into their dominion' and Qatar 'was designated a province in Najd under the control of the sanjak of Najd', and Jassim bin Mohammed was appointed kaymakam (the page's spelling).

wars.name: Qatari-Bahraini conflicts of 1847-1851

zones.text: the Qatari coast: Fuwayrit, Al Khor, Al Bidda

wars.outcome: The Al Khalifa won at Fuwayrit and razed Al Bidda (17 November 1847); Faisal's Najd took Qatar for a month after the Battle of Mesaimeer (June 1851) and made peace on 25 July.
wars.note: The Emirate of Nejd page gives the Mesaimeer settlement; the pages are silent on who won at Mesaimeer.

wars.name: Qatari-Bahraini War
wars.outcome: Al Wakrah and Al Bidda were sacked in 1867; the Battle of Damsah (late 1867 or June 1868) killed about 1,000; Pelly's 1868 settlement acknowledged Mohammed bin Thani.
wars.note: The page calls the attackers 'combined forces' (2,000 men); Bahrain's ally is not named in the extract read.

wars.name: Ottoman incorporation of Qatar
wars.outcome: No fighting: 100 Ottoman troops landed at Al Bidda in December 1871 at Jassim bin Mohammed's invitation and Qatar became a province in Najd by January 1872.
wars.note: The Al Wajbah episode of 1893 (the Qataris besieged the Ottomans in Al Bidda and they conceded defeat) lies outside this dossier's years.

certainty.note: The peninsula had no recognised boundary before the 1916 treaty (the History of Qatar page names only the Zubarah and Hawar disputes and a 1922 Uqair line); the coast and towns are the only certain land.

sources.title: History of Qatar
sources.note: The peninsula under the Al Khalifa, Doha and Al Bidda, Mohammed bin Thani, the wars of 1847-51 and 1867-68, Pelly 1868, the Ottoman landing and province of 1871-72, Al Wajbah 1893, 1913, 1916.

sources.title: Al Qasimi
sources.note: The Qawasim around Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, the 1820 General Maritime Treaty and 1853 peace: used to show that the northern patch of Cliopatria's shape is not Qatar; silent on Qatar.

sources.title: Emirate of Nejd
sources.note: Faisal's temporary dominion over Qatar after Mesaimeer (June 1851) and the peace of 25 July; silent on a Najdi south of the peninsula, on Buraimi and on the Trucial Coast.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Qatar Dynasty' row is two things: the Qatar peninsula (48 gazetteer cells, 1820-1894) and a patch of 17-19 cells around Ras al-Khaimah and Fujairah that stays in the row to 1904 and is its only content from 1895. The patch is not Qatari on any page (the Al Qasimi page puts the Qawasim, whose seat was Ras Al Khaimah, in that area; it never mentions Qatar), and Cliopatria has the Emirate of Nejd holding it in 1853-1855. The corrected shapes drop it; its owner (the Qawasim of Ras al-Khaimah and Sharjah, or the Trucial States row, which covers only 15 percent of the Ras al-Khaimah circle) is for the me-10 Trucial States dossier to settle. The southern 20 cells of the peninsula that Cliopatria gives the Emirate of Nejd in 1853-1872 contradict the Emirate of Nejd page (peace of July 1851: 'agreed to stop interfering in Qatari affairs'); the Ottoman dossier also draws all of Qatar for the Ottomans from 1873. Same state or not: the Wikidata id Q846 is shared with Cliopatria's 'Qatar' (1913-1915, dossier qatar) and 'State of Qatar' (1973-2024, state-of-qatar), written by other agents; the peninsula's polity is continuous in the pages (Al Thani since Mohammed bin Thani at Al Bidda in 1848, Ottoman province 1872-1913, British treaty 1916), so these are one state under three names; this dossier ends in January 1872 with the Ottoman province because the Ottoman dossier already owns the land from then, and the Ottoman renunciation of 1913 restarts the sheikhdom (qatar). Not settled: the date and extent of Al Khalifa overlordship (the pages give claims, tribute to Najd, the British recognition of Qatar as a dependent of Bahrain in 1861-62 and Najd's dominion of June-July 1851, no boundary); whether Qatar was a Bahraini vassal in 1820-1868 (a vassal event belongs in the Bahrain dossier); Cliopatria's 1853 southern cut-off (corrected). The autonomy the Al Thani kept as Ottoman kaymakams, and the defeat of the Ottomans at Al Wajbah in 1893, are on the History of Qatar page but fall outside the years of this dossier. The Al Khalifa counterpart is written house-of-khalifa (a slug another agent will create; Cliopatria's bahrain row ends in 1845).
